operatorProfile.notesBody: My work often sits at the meeting point of design and implementation. My focus is not the artefacts, but the systems that generate them - interface logic, motion templates, and production pipelines that scale while output remains consistent.

files.title: Operator Summary
files.body: Creative technologist working across product design, media pipelines, and technical prototyping. Leads briefs from specification through to delivery — coordinating external teams, building repeatable frameworks, and shipping across UI, motion, and AI-assisted production.

files.title: Working Style
files.body: Structured system design with iterative prototyping. Problems are reduced to inputs, constraints, and outputs, then rebuilt into reusable templates, rather than one-off solutions.

files.title: Current Focus
files.body: Video generation systems, AI-assisted development pipelines, interface architecture, and tools that reduce the distance between ideas and deployed products.

caseStudies.title: Case Studies
caseStudies.description: Each case exposes the system behind the output: inputs, constraints, pipelines, and repeatable structures.

projects.title: UNCX Video & 3D System
projects.shortDescription: End-to-end video production pipeline spanning Cinema 4D, After Effects, and Redshift — built for repeatable, high-frequency output.
projects.fullDescription: A modular production system covering 3D scene assembly in Cinema 4D, Redshift rendering, After Effects compositing, and templated timeline structures. Designed so that product launches, explainers, YouTube tutorials, and partner content could all ship from the same asset library without rebuilding from scratch each time.

overlaySections.title: Brief
overlaySections.body: UNCX Network needed a repeatable video system that could support product launches, explainer series, YouTube tutorials, and partner content — without rebuilding from scratch for every deliverable.

overlaySections.title: Problem Frame
overlaySections.body: Production was fragmented across freelancers and one-off files. No shared asset library, no consistent motion language, and no templated pipeline — every video started from zero.

overlaySections.title: System Design
overlaySections.body: Built a modular pipeline: reusable 3D scenes and camera rigs in Cinema 4D, Redshift lighting presets, templated After Effects compositions with established layout and edit conventions for consistent tone and pacing across formats.

overlaySections.title: Trade-offs
overlaySections.body: Time was the primary constraint — the operator managed the full production pipeline solo alongside other responsibilities. Early videos were over-scoped: lengthy scripts from the marketing team, unique animations per scene, and tight delivery timelines. Key pivots included introducing script length restrictions, stripping back unnecessary scenes, and replacing per-scene custom animations with categorised animation templates that could be reused across projects. The system evolved from complex one-off productions into a streamlined pipeline optimised for volume without sacrificing brand consistency.

overlaySections.title: Delivery
overlaySections.body: Delivered as a production system: Cinema 4D scene templates, After Effects project structures, Redshift material libraries, YouTube thumbnail templates, and established motion conventions baked into the project files.

overlaySections.title: Outcome
overlaySections.body: Cut production time significantly across campaigns. Enabled consistent, brand-aligned output regardless of content type — from 60-second launch trailers to long-form educational content for the Academy. The constraint-driven simplification became the system's strength: fewer unique elements, faster turnaround, more consistent output.

projects.title: Badger Club App
projects.shortDescription: Full-stack badge tracking platform with dark/light themes, role-based dashboards, Supabase backend, and Resend email integration.
projects.fullDescription: A multi-role product system managing badge progress tracking, leader administration, parent communication, and public-facing group pages. Built with React, Supabase, Resend email integration, and Cloudflare security. Supports dark and light themes with a structured database schema designed for scalable group management.

overlaySections.title: Brief
overlaySections.body: Build a badge tracking system that reduces admin overhead for group leaders while giving parents and children clear visibility into progress and achievements.

overlaySections.title: Problem Frame
overlaySections.body: Badge tracking was manual — spreadsheets, paper records, and inconsistent communication between leaders and parents. Leaders carried the full admin burden with no structured tooling.

overlaySections.title: System Design
overlaySections.body: Separated the system into operational layers: leader management dashboards for badge administration, parent-facing views for monitoring progress, child-friendly progress visualisation, and public group pages with Cloudflare messaging security.

overlaySections.title: Trade-offs
overlaySections.body: Initially envisioned as a multi-user platform with accounts for leaders, parents, and children. Legal and complexity constraints forced a pivot: the app became leader-only, with parent and child interactions designed to work without any account or sign-up. A full inbox and messaging system was also scoped but simplified — mirroring messages across a leader inbox, leader email, and parent email added significant complexity through Resend. The compromise: leaders manage messages via an in-app inbox with email notifications, while parents receive messages directly by email. Development was managed solo using AI-assisted tooling, with phases scoped as atomised tasks to prevent drift during autonomous builds.

overlaySections.title: Delivery
overlaySections.body: Full-stack implementation: React frontend with role-based routing, Supabase backend with structured schema, Google OAuth for authentication, Resend for transactional emails, and Cloudflare for security and performance.

overlaySections.title: Outcome
overlaySections.body: Eliminated manual tracking overhead. The constraint-driven simplification — leader-only accounts, no-signup parent access, streamlined messaging — produced a leaner product with fewer barriers to adoption. Created a scalable foundation with subscription-based monetisation and clear paths for feature expansion.

projects.title: UNCX Company Rebrand
projects.shortDescription: Two-phase rebrand: an initial name and logo overhaul in 2022, followed by a full brand system and website redesign in 2024 — briefed and spec'd by the operator, executed with an external team, then finished in-house.
projects.fullDescription: The UNCX Network rebrand happened in two stages. In 2022, the operator led a solo rebrand covering the company name change and primary logo. In 2024, a second phase brought in an external team who worked from the operator's brief and design specification to deliver a full brand system and website redesign in Figma. The operator then brought the work in-house, completing the content, layout, and graphics across 10+ pages.

overlaySections.title: Brief
overlaySections.body: Evolve the UNCX Network brand across two phases — an initial name and logo change, then a comprehensive brand system and website redesign across the multi-chain DeFi ecosystem.

overlaySections.title: Problem Frame
overlaySections.body: The existing brand was inconsistent — different visual treatments per product, no systemised colour or typography logic, and marketing outputs that didn't align with the product UI. The first rebrand addressed the name and mark; the second tackled the full system.

overlaySections.title: System Design
overlaySections.body: Wrote the brief and design specification for the 2024 rebrand. An external team delivered the brand system and website redesign in Figma. The operator then brought the project in-house, completing content, layout refinements, and graphic production across all product pages.

overlaySections.title: Trade-offs
overlaySections.body: The first phase in 2022 was driven by urgency — a legal copyright issue required a swift name and identity change with minimal runway. The second phase in 2024 introduced a different constraint: the external team delivered strong initial concepts, colour direction, and brand foundations, but struggled to populate the website designs with accurate product content. They understood the design system but lacked domain knowledge of the products. Hand-holding the content population wasn't sustainable, so the operator brought the project in-house — completing the website designs, content, and graphics using the external team's guidelines as the foundation. The next phase of resistance came trying to implement the designs consistently across all the development subteams.

overlaySections.title: Delivery
overlaySections.body: Delivered brand guidelines, Figma component libraries, website page designs across 10+ product pages, marketing visual templates, and motion style references.

overlaySections.title: Outcome
overlaySections.body: Achieved consistent visual output across all platforms and products. The split approach — external team for brand foundations, in-house for product-specific execution — became the working model. Brand alignment across product teams took longer than the design work itself, but the system now supports coherent output without design drift.

projects.title: Noticia Lingo App
projects.shortDescription: Language learning app with an AI-assisted classroom, real news articles, Google authentication, Supabase backend, and structured quiz flows.
projects.fullDescription: A language learning platform that transforms live news content into structured learning experiences. Built with React, Supabase, and Google OAuth — featuring article-based lessons, interactive quizzes, a learner dashboard, and a settings system. Designed to replace static flashcard approaches with contextual, real-world content.

overlaySections.title: Brief
overlaySections.body: Build a language learning system that uses real-world news content instead of static lessons — making vocabulary acquisition contextual and engaging.

overlaySections.title: Problem Frame
overlaySections.body: Traditional language apps rely on decontextualised flashcards and repetitive drills. Learners lose motivation because the content feels disconnected from real usage.

overlaySections.title: System Design
overlaySections.body: Content pipeline: ingest news articles, extract vocabulary, generate contextual quizzes, and structure progressive difficulty. User system: Google OAuth, learner profiles, progress tracking, and configurable settings.

overlaySections.title: Trade-offs
overlaySections.body: The primary constraint has been lesson complexity. Initial development using AI tooling produced oversimplified quiz questions rather than the pure-function puzzle systems the operator had specified — lessons that work contextually against any news article, not static question-and-answer pairs. The pivot: expanding the roadmap into granular build phases, constructing each of the 8–10 lesson types step by step with greater complexity control. Technical implementation — Google OAuth, Supabase integration — proved straightforward by comparison. The system is currently focused on Spanish to validate the lesson architecture before introducing multi-language complexity, where each lesson type will need to be adapted per language.

overlaySections.title: Delivery
overlaySections.body: Working prototype with React frontend, Supabase backend, Google authentication, structured article reading flow, quiz system, and learner dashboard.

overlaySections.title: Outcome
overlaySections.body: Demonstrated a scalable learning system driven by live content. The shift from AI-generated simple quizzes to operator-designed pure-function lesson types produced a more robust foundation. Active development with plans for multi-language expansion once the core 8–10 lesson types are validated in Spanish.

projects.title: UNCX Academy Brand & Platform
projects.shortDescription: Educational platform brand and design system — logotype, component library, article system, video pages, and glossary for DeFi learning.
projects.fullDescription: Brand and platform design for UNCX Academy. The operator wrote the brief and design specification, then an external team delivered the initial design system — custom logotype, component library, and page templates. The operator brought the project in-house, completing the designs for article categorisation, video learning pages, glossary, integrations hub, and about page ready for in-house development. The operator's video production system was integrated to produce the platform's educational video library.

overlaySections.title: Brief
overlaySections.body: Design a complete educational platform brand and UI for UNCX Academy — covering identity, page designs, content structure, and a reusable component system.

overlaySections.title: Problem Frame
overlaySections.body: DeFi education content was scattered across blog posts, YouTube videos, and documentation with no unified platform, no consistent visual language, and no structured learning progression.

overlaySections.title: System Design
overlaySections.body: Wrote the brief and design specification. An external team delivered the logotype, brand identity, and modular Figma component library. The operator then brought the project in-house, refining content structure across articles, videos, glossary entries, and integrations — each with its own page template and navigation pattern.

overlaySections.title: Trade-offs
overlaySections.body: Having navigated similar external team constraints during the rebrand, the operator applied a more structured handoff process for the Academy. The external design team delivered strong foundational work — logotype, component library, and page templates — but lacked the product context to complete content-specific designs. The operator designed the hero graphics, page visuals, and layout specifics, then handed off finished designs to an in-house developer who built the site and backend CMS. The video production system integrated seamlessly as both the platform and video content were built from the same brand specification. Beyond the platform launch, the operator also produces all article header banners for the marketing team's ongoing content output.

overlaySections.title: Delivery
overlaySections.body: Complete Figma design system: logotype, component library, page templates for Main, Articles, Videos, Glossary, Integrations, and About. Finished in-house and prepared for development handoff with supporting brand guidelines.

overlaySections.title: Outcome
overlaySections.body: Enabled UNCX Network to launch a structured education platform aligned with the parent brand. The video production system fed directly into the Academy's content library, and the operator's ongoing production of article banners, page graphics, and video content created a single-source creative pipeline across the entire platform.

projects.title: UNCX Unified Menu
projects.shortDescription: Cross-product navigation component system with variable-driven Figma prototypes, research-backed hierarchy, and scalable state logic.
projects.fullDescription: A unified menu system designed to work across UNCX's entire product suite. Built as a variable-driven Figma component with researched navigation patterns, prototype states (open/closed), configurable content slots, and a scalable hierarchy that adapts to different product contexts.

overlaySections.title: Brief
overlaySections.body: Design a unified navigation component that could work across all UNCX Network products and platforms — replacing inconsistent platform menus with a single scalable system.

overlaySections.title: Problem Frame
overlaySections.body: Each UNCX Network product had its own navigation pattern. Users moving between EVM tools, Solana products, Academy, and the homepage encountered different menu structures, creating cognitive overhead and inconsistent UX.

overlaySections.title: System Design
overlaySections.body: Researched navigation patterns and hierarchy models. Designed a component-based menu with configurable content slots, variable-driven Figma states, and a scalable hierarchy that adapts per product context.

overlaySections.title: Trade-offs
overlaySections.body: The project is on hold due to a shift in development priorities. The core design challenge was fitting multiple products and sub-brands into a single menu structure that remained efficient and navigable. An additional constraint was that the products are highly specialised — the menu needed to be mildly educational, helping users understand what each product does without slowing down experienced users. The main design compromise centred on hierarchy: several products generate significantly more revenue than others and needed visual priority, without devaluing the rest of the ecosystem.

overlaySections.title: Delivery
overlaySections.body: Delivered a Figma design system component with documented states, variables, content slot patterns, and implementation specifications for the development team.

overlaySections.title: Outcome
overlaySections.body: Delivered a complete design system ready for implementation. The hierarchy problem — balancing revenue-generating products against the broader ecosystem — was resolved by establishing definitive levels of hierarchy and de-prioritising non-value generating menu options. Currently on hold pending a shift in development priorities.

projects.title: UNCX App Prototyping
projects.shortDescription: Rapid prototyping across token minting, launchpad flows, Telegram bots, NFT minting, and full launchpad concepts — from wireframes to interactive concepts.
projects.fullDescription: A body of product concepting work spanning multiple UNCX Network features: token minter prototyping, launchpad UI components, Telegram chatbot and presale app flows, NFT minting interfaces, stealth launch concepts, and full launchpad concepts.

overlaySections.title: Brief
overlaySections.body: Rapidly prototype and validate product concepts across UNCX Network's feature pipeline — covering token minting, launchpad flows, Telegram integrations, and NFT tooling.

overlaySections.title: Problem Frame
overlaySections.body: New product features were being scoped without visual validation. Developers were building from text specs, leading to misalignment between design intent and implementation.

overlaySections.title: System Design
overlaySections.body: A broad range of product concepts and prototypes spanning different stages and purposes. Some were built and shipped — token minter flows, launchpad components, and Telegram bot interactions. Others remained as design explorations — stealth launch interfaces, NFT minting tools, and full launchpad concepts. Each served to validate direction, align stakeholders, or define scope before committing development resources.

overlaySections.title: Trade-offs
overlaySections.body: A recurring constraint across all concepts was incomplete requirements — specifications arrived gradually as projects developed, often requiring rework of existing prototypes. This made component-based design systems essential: rebuilding from reusable parts reduced the cost of iteration. Figma's later introduction of the variables system further reduced component creation overhead. A foundational part of each project was creating FigJam flow diagrams for novel product processes. These weren't problems with established UX conventions to reference — they required working out how the interactions should function from first principles.

overlaySections.title: Delivery
overlaySections.body: Delivered Figma prototypes for each feature area: token minting (blueprint and standard), launchpad components, Telegram bot/app flows, NFT minting interfaces, stealth launch admin, and full launchpad flow diagrams.

overlaySections.title: Outcome
overlaySections.body: Closed the gap between product specs and development handoff. The component-first approach meant that incomplete or shifting requirements — a constant across a five-year span of prototyping — could be absorbed without starting from scratch. Stakeholders could validate features visually before committing development resources, reducing rework and accelerating shipping.
